facts.fact: Construction of Phase 2 of the National Fibre Optic Backbone Infrastructure Project, a 721.5 km fibre network covering 15 major cities in the northern, eastern and southern regions, had commenced by September 2020 under a Huawei contract signed 11 April 2019 and financed by a China Eximbank RMB 207 million loan (AidData record).

facts.fact: Minister of Communication, Technology and Innovation Salima Bah said the national fibre backbone had been expanded to 14 of the country's 16 districts (article of 2026-05-05; as_of is the article date, which gives no earlier date).

Minister Salima Bah said at the NatCA headquarters commissioning that 14 of 16 districts are now connected by fibre (SLENA report of 2026-04-17; as_of is the report date, which gives no earlier date).

note: Minister cites an over 75% rise in fibre backbone penetration since 2018, with no places, regions or km, so reach is not stated; Guinea link is cross-border and not described as part of the national backbone; open access applies to a 5G network, not the backbone.

facts.fact: Minister Salima Bah said the fibre backbone grew from 8 to 14 districts through a 1,641 km fibre rollout.
Minister Salima Bah told Parliament's ICT committee on 29 April 2026 that the fibre backbone has been expanded to 14 of Sierra Leone's 16 districts, with work under way to reach Falaba and Karene.
CSquared says its fibre backbone connects international cable landing points to inland markets across Burkina Faso, Mali, Guinea, Sierra Leone and Liberia.
CSquared describes itself as a neutral open-access wholesale infrastructure company whose backbone gives operators access to international routes.
